## Requirements: Git capability — read-only GitHub repository context

### Problem and scope

Nession already has a read-only, Session-scoped local Git capability:

```text
Authorized Session -> Agent WorkdirResolver -> nession-git / GitCmd
                   -> git.status/diff/root/log/commit/branches/worktrees
                   -> GitPlugin -> Git capability -> Git Workspace
```

The missing slice is **repository hosting context for that same Git repository**: GitHub Issues, Pull Requests, Actions/workflow runs and the current branch's open PR. These are hosting-provider facts, **not native Git objects**. Keep **one product-level Git capability**, with separate local-Git and hosting-provider ownership. This Issue owns a **read-only GitHub v1** plus its minimal Git Workspace presentation, not a generic GitHub client or a redefinition of Workspace.

**Current-source baseline (2026-10-28, `main@54bac41eea41af9aa3ae4919f4bcb104e6554534`):**
- `crates/nession-git/src/runtime/cmd.rs` owns the sole git subprocess chokepoint; `crates/nession-git/src/agent.rs` injects `WorkdirResolver`, without accepting client-supplied cwd.
- `web/src/capabilities/git/components/GitWorkspace.tsx` has four local sections; `GitPlugin.ts` binds existing `git.*` units. `git.commit` means **read-only commit detail** (#1009), not creating a commit.
- No `crates/nession-github`, no `github.*` Protocol Units, no `e2e/acceptance/cases/1290`; both Agent Dockerfiles install `git` but not `gh`. The GitHub slice is not implemented; no SC is accepted.

Related: #750 (read-only Git), #826 (capability depth), #846, #1008, #1009, #678 (Protocol Units), #845 (separate local Git mutation), #2469 (Session ownership), #1474/#2323 (acceptance).

### Goals

1. Derive the GitHub repository **only from the caller's authorized, live Agent Session repository** and its Git remotes.
2. Add a bounded, read-only GitHub provider for Issues, PRs, Actions and current-branch PR association.
3. Keep local Git functional when GitHub is missing, unauthenticated, offline, denied or rate-limited.
4. Keep the Git capability's typed API reusable and independently versioned without giving GitHub a second top-level capability.
5. Present the data in the existing Git Workspace with repository/hosting hierarchy, without a new global navigation concept.

### Native Git/GitHub data boundary and Work composition (owner clarification, 2026-11-06)

**Git / GitHub is a complete, standalone native-data Workspace capability. Work (#2541) is a separate capability that may consume its authorized data through an adapter; the two do not compete for ownership.** This supersedes any prior interpretation that Github Issue/PR rendering should move out of Git because WorkContract exists.

- **Git** owns presentation of native local repository state (changes, diffs, branches, history, worktrees) and native GitHub hosting state (repository identity, Issues, PRs and Actions), with GitHub's own object names, bodies, metadata, lifecycle and source links. A generic GitHub Issue must render as a GitHub Issue even if it is not a Nession Requirement, cannot be parsed as a WorkContract or has no Work binding.
- **Work** owns only derived Nession work semantics (WorkContract, Criteria, Thread/Event projection, Execution and Verification). No WorkContract-specific parsing, acceptance status, inferred criteria or task lifecycle is introduced into the Git/GitHub UI or its public `github.*` DTOs.
- A **reusable typed GitHub read client** may be consumed from a Work SourceAdapter under that adapter's independently validated Workspace/SourceBinding authority; this is dependency reuse, **not** Git UI reuse. The Session-bound `github.*` operations in this Issue must continue to resolve repository identity from the authorized active Agent Session and never become an arbitrary owner/repo browser for Work.
- **GitHub raw source truth is not Nession work authority.** GitHub labels, checkboxes, comment status, reviews and Actions conclusions remain native provider facts. Interpreting these as Contract state, trusted criterion Pass or Agent execution belongs to #2541 and the relevant existing verification/execution owners, never to #1290.
- One **product-level Git capability** can use distinct `git.*` and `github.*` transport providers. Provider independence must not create a second GitHub Capsule item or a global GitHub application.

**Read-only native depth and delivery control:** v1 remains the currently accepted bounded Issues/PRs **summary → full body/detail** and Actions **workflow/run summary** contract (SC-07..09). Reading Issue comments, PR changed-file lists/patches, review conversations, and Actions jobs/logs is legitimate **native GitHub capability** work, not Work functionality. Review recommendation: prioritize **paginated Issue comments and PR Files/Diff** as the next explicit read-only depth; review threads and jobs/logs follow only when justified. They are **design candidates, not silently added closure obligations**: before making them mandatory, revise the affected SC/Plan, bound the API/byte/pagination semantics, and synchronize the linked Web/App prototype. Do not use these candidates to block the currently approved v1's Acceptance.

**Prototype impact:** this clarification adds no new required screen, navigation or interaction to the approved v1 prototype; the existing Git capability prototype remains the design reference for current SCs. Future comment/file-depth approval requires a synchronized scenario/prototype revision, distinct from the production acceptance record.

### Explicit non-goals

- AI Workspace Scenes, intent routing, AI Conversation component protocol or other AI-native UI work (#2221/#2254 own those separately).
- GitHub mutations: create/edit/comment/close Issue or PR, review/merge, workflow dispatch/rerun/cancel, checkout PR.
- Local Git write operations (#845 and its separate authorization/write boundary).
- Arbitrary GitHub owner/repo browser; user-specified API endpoints; OAuth/credential-management UI.
- GitLab/Gitea/Bitbucket provider implementations, Releases/Discussions/Projects, full review timeline, workflow logs or a GitHub web clone.
- Polling all remote state in the background; adding any Terminal-local Git Peek or GitHub preview surface. Git hosting lists belong to Git Workspace.

### Architecture and ownership

```text
Git capability (single product capability / Workspace entry)
  ├─ Local Repository
  │   GitPlugin -> git.* units -> nession-git -> GitCmd -> git
  └─ GitHub hosting context
      GitHub read facade -> github.* units -> nession-github
                                             -> typed GithubClient -> read-only GitHub API
```

- `nession-git` remains Git-specific and GitHub-agnostic. Introduce a **typed repository context/remote resolver** through the existing GitCmd only; no second `Command::new("git")`. Do not build an unrelated repository abstraction framework.
- The Agent's Session layer owns **Session identity, live cwd acquisition and authorization** (align with #2469); Git repository root/branch/remotes are resolved through `nession-git`. The GitHub provider receives only that verified typed context.
- `nession-github` owns GitHub-specific host identity, read-only client, API DTO/normalization, authentication boundary, failures, rate limiting and request budgets. It must **not** import Git Workspace/UI concerns and must not access tmux or run git itself.
- Agent transport may register a `github.*` provider/extension independently, but **the frontend presents one Git capability**. GitHub's frontend facade stays under `web/src/capabilities/git/`; never register GitHub as a competing top-level Workspace capability.
- Server relays typed calls and enforces caller/Session routing authorization, never owns/stores GitHub credentials or interprets GitHub APIs. An Agent must recheck Session scope rather than trusting client-supplied IDs as authority.
- Keep existing `git.*` contracts and their read-only semantics unchanged. New provider-owned `github.*` contracts use the version-directory/manifest/codegen mechanism (#678).

### Repository identity and remote resolution

```text
Authorized Agent+Session -> live cwd -> GitCmd repo root
                         -> branch / upstream / verified remotes
                         -> selected GitHub remote
                         -> { host, owner, repo, remote_name, branch? }
```

- Parse fetch/push Git remote forms safely, including `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`, `https://github.com/owner/repo.git`, and `ssh://git@github.com/owner/repo.git`; recognize credential-bearing URLs only to redact/reject sensitive portions. No shell interpolation or arbitrary args.
- Default remote: current branch's configured upstream remote **if valid GitHub** -> `origin` **if valid GitHub** -> sole valid GitHub remote -> typed `ambiguous_remote`. Detached HEAD has no branch PR association.
- If ambiguous, Web may select a **remote_name discovered by the Agent for that Session**, not host/owner/repo. Re-resolve that name on every request; if it has disappeared/changed, invalidate selection and ask for a new choice.
- Keep GitHub Enterprise host in canonical identity, but **recognition is not authorization**: API target hosts must be `github.com` or explicitly configured/approved Enterprise hosts with verified per-host auth. Unknown host, SSH alias, malformed URL or disallowed redirect must not result in an authenticated network call.
- Normalize `owner/repo` and branch/head references with exact identity; do not infer current-branch PR by branch name alone. For forks, compare selected repository, PR head repository owner and `head.ref`; absence/ambiguity is not a match.
- Fetch and push remotes may differ; expose the selected hosting identity clearly. No secret-bearing raw URL enters protocol, display, diagnostics, logs or cache keys.

### GitHub client and authentication policy

**v1 decision:** define a typed `GithubClient` with fixed, read-only operations; the implementation may use bounded `gh api` GET requests where the Agent actually has `gh` and host-specific authentication, or a typed HTTP GET client with Agent-owned credentials. Choose/document one executable backend for initial delivery; **no implicit switching to anonymous access** or leaking secrets to Server/Web. The same allowlist, timeout, byte, redirect and error contracts apply to either backend.

- Allowlist GitHub GET operations and typed filters, not arbitrary CLI arguments, GraphQL text or request paths supplied by Web. Explicitly prohibit POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE in v1.
- Disable prompts/pagers, interactive auth and shell execution; bound process/runtime, response bytes, total request duration, page size, concurrency and retry budget. Never log effective auth headers, sensitive URL fields, CLI env or raw stderr.
- Agent host `git` availability, `gh` executable availability and API authentication are **three different facts**. Both `Dockerfile.agent` and `Dockerfile.agent.prebuilt` currently lack `gh`; if choosing `gh`, package and verify it in both actual runtimes (plus documented native host requirements). CI having `gh` is not proof.
- SSH access to a Git remote does **not** prove permission to read GitHub REST APIs. Private repositories must not silently fall back to public/anonymous results after an auth failure.
- Enterprise host, proxy and redirect validation must prevent unauthorized host access or SSRF/credential forwarding. Unknown/unsupported hosts have a typed unavailable outcome.
- Failures: `not_a_repository`, `no_github_remote`, `ambiguous_remote`, `host_not_allowed`, `client_unavailable`, `not_authenticated`, `access_denied`, `rate_limited`, `network_unavailable`, `timeout`, `api_error`, `malformed_response`. Preserve sanitized machine-readable codes and safe short human messages. Partial vs empty vs unavailable must remain distinguishable.

### Protocol Units and API model

Provider-owned, independent v1 units:

```text
github.repository      -> selected identity, discovered choices, availability/auth state
github.issues          -> bounded issue summaries page + filters
github.issue_detail    -> one selected Issue, full body/metadata/source URL
github.pull_requests   -> bounded PR summaries page + current-branch relation
github.pull_request_detail -> one selected PR, full body/metadata/head/base
github.workflows       -> bounded workflow list + selected latest-run summaries
```

A separate `github.workflow_runs` unit is optional **only if** the implementation needs independent pagination/detail; do not add it by default. Requests carry `session`, optional discovered `remote_name`, typed bounded `filters` and opaque `continuation`. `agent_id` is transport routing, never a provider-selected repository. Results carry selected host/owner/repo identity and explicit `next_cursor`/end; unknown contract versions fail through normal protocol negotiation. No arbitrary repository path, GitHub endpoint or API query parameter on the wire.

**Issues**: default open; summary fields number/title/state/author/labels/assignees/updated_at/url; open/closed/all; safely filter PR-shaped issue API records within provider. **When a row is selected**, request `github.issue_detail` by validated Issue number scoped to the already resolved Agent Session + repository. The detail returns typed full Markdown body and canonical source URL with explicit loading/not-found/permission/error states.

**Pull Requests**: default open; summary fields number/title/state/draft/author/head/base/updated_at/url; current-branch association is identity-checked and explicitly `matched | none | ambiguous`, not a branch-name guess. When a PR row is selected, request `github.pull_request_detail` for its real body/metadata/head/base/source URL. Do **not** eagerly fetch full bodies for all list rows or expand N items into N+1 detail calls. Issue/PR detail endpoints remain fixed, GET-only, no mutation or GitHub-host/user path input from Web.

**Reader interaction and data consistency**: list response is bounded summaries; detail is a separate, lazy, bounded, cancellable/identity-guarded read with its own selected-number key. Search/filter/pagination and selected row are preserved across detail open/close; a newly selected row supersedes the previous request. On Session/remote/repository switch, discard prior list **and detail** data, not just its selected title. Render Markdown safely (escape arbitrary HTML, sanitize links/assets), and expose a validated external GitHub read-only source link. List/reader show status, author, timestamps, labels or PR branch metadata. No inline comments/edits/merge in v1.

**Actions**: workflows with name/path/enabled state and bounded latest-run data (status, conclusion, branch, sha, event, timestamp, URL). Do not collapse `queued` or `in_progress` into `failure`, or `No runs yet` into API error. Distinguish **repository latest** from **current-branch latest**; a green main run cannot imply that a feature branch passed. Avoid one unbounded run query per workflow: fetch only the visible bounded workflow page, use limited concurrency and lazily resolve extra run data if necessary.

### Cache, freshness and consistency

- **No interval polling**. Request when GitHub depth/selected view becomes visible, on explicit Refresh or filter/page changes. Hidden views and ordinary file-save invalidation trigger no GitHub API calls.
- A small **in-memory, bounded and short-lived** read cache/request dedup is permitted; its key includes Agent, authorized Session, resolved repository/remote, GitHub host/auth identity, operation/filter/page and branch where relevant. Never persist tokens or share private results across identities.
- Re-resolve Session cwd/remote identity for each authoritative request. A change of Session, cwd/repository, remote, branch or authenticated host invalidates relevant data and in-flight responses. Apply generation/request-key guards before updating UI; old replies cannot overwrite current content.
- Respect rate limits with bounded retries/backoff and user-triggered retry; no retries that generate GitHub Actions API storms. Explicitly distinguish cached/fresh, exhausted/empty and error outcomes.

### Git Workspace presentation (bounded to this plugin)

```text
Git Workspace
  Repository — Changes / History / Branches / Worktrees
  GitHub · host/owner/repo — Issues / Pull Requests / Actions
```

**Capsule integration decision (owner update 2026-10-28):** The previous `Terminal Capsule → Git Peek → Open Workspace` interaction is **superseded for this Git capability**. Do **not** use, require, expand or reimplement Git Peek as a product step. When the Git capability is selected through the current Capsule capability/navigation entry, the Git Workspace opens **directly**, with the authorized Session/repository/worktree and any applicable resource focus preserved. This is a Git capability integration requirement, not an authorization to redesign the global Capsule, introduce a separate Git destination button, or alter unrelated capabilities.

Current `main` still contains `web/src/capabilities/git/components/GitProjection.tsx`, the `gitProjection` registration in `contribution.tsx`, and the generic `PeekHost` path. Those are **legacy implementation facts, not acceptance targets**. During #1290 Git integration, migrate/bypass the Git-specific legacy entry/projection so it no longer intervenes between Capsule selection and Git Workspace; do not remove the shared Peek machinery used by other capabilities as part of this Issue. In particular, the historical Peek portions of `docs/design/capability-emergence.md`, `docs/design/design-system/patterns/context-capsule.md` and #1347 must **not** be used to reinstate a Git Peek requirement; their global supersession/cleanup belongs to the owning Capsule design work.

Use the existing Git Workspace content, not a second global capability or seven flat tabs. Web/App share semantic selection; remote selector contains **only Agent-discovered candidates**. On ambiguity/auth/offline, show a scoped actionable explanation while Local Repository continues working. Preserve focus/return, bounded scroll and current Capsule overlay/clearance semantics per `docs/design/design-system/patterns/workspace-navigation.md`. GitHub Issues/PR/Actions never materialize as an extra Terminal Capsule surface.

**Issue/PR list → detail layout (2026-10-28 prototype decision):** on Web/wide layouts, keep a **bounded scrollable summary list** at left (approx. one-third width) and a **separately scrollable full-body reader** at right. Selecting another row updates the reader without leaving Git Workspace; for long descriptions, a **Focus reading** control may collapse the list while keeping selection/filter state. On App/narrow screens, the first level is the list; selecting a row pushes a **full-width detail view**, with an explicit **Back to list** that restores previous filtering, search, scroll and selection. The list/reader must not scroll as one enormous page or hide its last row beneath the Capsule. Do not invent a new top-level Issue/PR capability, a modal, a Git Peek, or write controls. The threshold and exact visual tokens are design refinements, not hardcoded protocol semantics.

### Interactive prototype — Git capability / GitHub context (#1290)

- **Direct interactive HTML preview (Pages HTTPS/manifest SHA not yet verified):** https://bestnathan.github.io/nession/prototypes/git-github-1290/index.html
- **Pinned immutable source:** https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/bcb608d223c971d6062d295bac14caf739ea144e/git-github-1290/index.html
- **Pinned UX walkthrough and layout decisions:** https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/bcb608d223c971d6062d295bac14caf739ea144e/git-github-1290/README.md
- **Recorded source fixtures:** https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/bcb608d223c971d6062d295bac14caf739ea144e/git-github-1290/fixtures.js
- **Native prototype library:** https://bestnathan.github.io/nession/#/prototypes
- **Branch and publication:** shared history-isolated `prototype@bcb608d223c971d6062d295bac14caf739ea144e` (fast-forward only; main/production untouched).
- **Design behavior:** current Capsule selects Git → Git Workspace directly (**no Git Peek**); Repository and GitHub remain within one capability. GitHub Issues/PRs use a desktop split list + full Markdown reader (independent scroll), optional Focus reading, and a mobile list → full-width detail → Back to list transition. State/filter/search/selection survive navigation. Actions scope, remotes, unavailable and empty cases remain inspectable.
- **Real read-only source data:** public **BestNathan/nession** Issue [#1290](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/issues/1290), [#2514](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/issues/2514), [#2323](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/issues/2323), plus open/draft/merged PR [#2229](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/pull/2229), [#2222](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/pull/2222), [#2518](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/pull/2518), [#2522](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/pull/2522); titles/states/metadata/descriptive Markdown are **recorded GitHub snapshots captured 2026-10-28**, not live API. The mock Session and its branch, local Git, Actions, fork remotes, provider/network/auth failure scenarios and refresh are synthetic. The simulated fork explicitly **does not display upstream real snapshots under the wrong repo identity**.
- **Verification:** latest published branch files and pinned SHA verified through GitHub reads; standalone JS compiled/executed with deterministic mock DOM: **31/31 interactive assertions passed**, including real fixture details, list/reader selection, Focus reading, mobile detail/back state, filter/search, host/fork data isolation, and fallback. This is **not** a real browser/e2e/trusted Acceptance run. Public Pages HTTPS and `prototypes/manifest.json` parity remain **unverified**, so do not describe the preview as confirmed live until both are checked.
- **Status:** Source artifact published, UX review and real desktop/mobile browser checks pending; **all 25 production SCs remain Pending**.

### Test and failure matrix

- **Resolver:** repo/non-repo, nested cwd, Session cd, detached HEAD, worktree, no remote, origin fork/canonical upstream, ambiguous remotes, renamed/deleted remote, SSH/scp/HTTPS, .git, malformed/credential-bearing URL, GitLab-only repo, Enterprise allowlist/denial.
- **Provider/security:** absent executable, wrong host auth, private repo allow/deny, rate limit and retry-after, timeout/offline, malformed response, forbidden endpoints/methods, untrusted redirect, sanitized errors/argv/env, concurrent sessions with different credentials.
- **Data:** no/many Issues/PRs, filters, draft/merged, full selected-record detail body/metadata, Markdown safety, empty/detail-not-found/loading/error, selected record switch and stale-result rejection, fork-head identity, workflow disabled/no runs/queued/running/success/failure, repository-vs-branch run scope, paginated end/continuation, bounded page/bytes/concurrency.
- **Freshness:** Session/repo/remote/branch/auth switches midflight, stale requests/caches, hidden view inactivity, save-invalidation separation, duplicate visible requests and no polling.
- **UI/integration:** GitHub failure with local Git still working; independent desktop list/detail scrolling and Focus reading; mobile push-detail + Back to list preserving selection/search/filter and bottom Capsule clearance; safe real-record link; real Agent runtime packaging/auth, exact-SHA bounded cross-component Tests.

### Knowledge Impact

- Decision: Create
- Related knowledge: #750, #678, #1290 and canonical Git capability docs; look up existing `git` topic in the `knowledge` branch before publication and update an existing canonical article instead of duplicating if one exists.
- Reason: Hosting-provider trust/identity, GitCmd reuse and GitHub protocol ownership are durable engineering boundaries.
- Owner and timing: #1290 implementation/reviewer before acceptance closure; governed knowledge-branch write, not untrusted PR execution.
- Evidence: Accepted exact-SHA source/SC evidence plus knowledge commit and global CHANGELOG link; Pending until implemented.

### Success Criteria

- [ ] SC-01 One Git capability exposes Local Repository and GitHub hosting context for the active Session; no second top-level capability is registered.
- [x] SC-02 Local Git remains in nession-git/GitCmd; GitHub authentication, network and API access have an independently auditable nession-github client boundary.
- [x] SC-03 Repository/remote discovery reuses the existing GitCmd chokepoint and introduces no second direct Git subprocess path.
- [ ] SC-04 Every GitHub target is resolved from an authorized Agent Session and its live repository; clients cannot name arbitrary owner/repo/path/host.
- [ ] SC-05 Branch upstream -> origin -> sole-GitHub-remote fallback and validated discovered-remote selection cover fork/upstream and ambiguous cases.
- [ ] SC-06 Supported HTTPS/scp-style SSH/ssh:// remotes normalize to host/owner/repo without leaking URL credentials or accepting untrusted host aliases.
- [ ] SC-07 Issues list provides scoped bounded summaries, open/closed/all filters, pagination/end and typed errors; selecting an Issue fetches its full, safely rendered, read-only detail with verified repository identity and source URL, without N+1 list fetches.
- [ ] SC-08 PR list provides bounded summaries and exact repository/head-owner/head-ref current-branch relation; selecting a PR fetches its full, safely rendered, read-only detail/body/head/base/source URL without eagerly requesting all bodies.
- [ ] SC-09 Actions read operations return bounded workflow and latest-run information with distinct queued/in_progress/completed/conclusion, disabled and no-runs states.
- [x] SC-10 No Issues/PR/Actions mutation protocol, client invocation or UI control is introduced.
- [ ] SC-11 Real Agent authentication never exposes credentials through transport payloads, Server/Web, persisted state, provider errors or diagnostics.
- [ ] SC-12 Missing client, unauthenticated host, forbidden repo, rate limit, network error, no remote and ambiguous remotes are distinct typed outcomes.
- [ ] SC-13 In an integrated Agent/Server/Web run, GitHub unavailability or API failure leaves existing Changes/History/Branches/Worktrees functional.
- [ ] SC-14 Git Workspace groups Repository and GitHub depths without seven flat peer tabs; Web and App share meaning and retain focus.
- [ ] SC-15 Selecting Git via the current Capsule entry opens Git Workspace directly with the same Session/repository/worktree and applicable focus; no Git-specific Peek, intermediate projection or extra Capsule surface is required or displayed.
- [ ] SC-16 Only visible GitHub views request data on entry, explicit refresh or filter/page change; local file invalidation and hidden views cause no GitHub API storms.
- [ ] SC-17 Session/cwd/repository/remote/branch/auth-context changes cannot publish stale in-flight results into the new identity.
- [ ] SC-18 All provider operations enforce endpoint/method allowlists, per-page/output/time budgets, bounded concurrency and explicit pagination/end.
- [x] SC-19 Provider-owned github.* Protocol Units are independently versioned, manifested and code-generated; generated Web bindings are authoritative.
- [ ] SC-20 Real integrated Web/App browser acceptance covers unavailable/auth/fork states, Issues/PR/Actions, desktop independently scrollable list+detail with Focus reading, mobile list→detail→back preserving filters/selection/scroll and Capsule clearance, and absence of mutation controls.
- [x] SC-21 Canonical Git capability and packaging documentation describes Local Git vs hosting provider ownership, read-only GitHub flow and failure behavior.
- [ ] SC-22 Untrusted remote URLs, custom hosts, redirects and CLI/API arguments cannot cause credential-bearing requests to an unapproved host or arbitrary endpoint.
- [ ] SC-23 Actions latest run is explicitly scoped (repository-wide versus current branch); another branch's success is never presented as current-branch success.
- [ ] SC-24 Short-lived, auth-scoped cache and in-flight dedup never cross Session/repository/remote/credential identities and invalidate correctly on identity changes.
- [ ] SC-25 Actual supported Agent runtimes prove packaged client/auth availability or return an honest unavailable state, without depending on CI-host gh installation.
